questions.q: Under SPP Doc 201, what is the term for the service that involves identifying potential sites and evaluating them for their suitability for the project?
questions.n: This service helps the owner determine the best location by analyzing factors like topography, utilities, and land use.

questions.q: Which service involves the systematic process of identifying the requirements of the project, including the user's needs and spatial relationships?
questions.n: Often called 'problem seeking,' programming defines the spatial and functional requirements of the project.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a Feasibility Study in the pre-design phase (SPP Doc 201)?
o: To determine if the project is viable based on technical, financial, and legal considerations
To apply for the building permit
To create the final floor plans
questions.n: It assesses if a project is 'doable' and profitable before the owner commits significant capital.

questions.q: Which service involves evaluating the 'Highest and Best Use' of a property to maximize its potential value?
questions.n: This study analyzes how to best utilize a specific plot of land within the constraints of law and market demand.

questions.q: How is an architect usually compensated for pre-design services where the time spent is the primary variable?
questions.n: MDPE is ideal for services where the scope is not yet fixed and depends on the time of the professionals involved.

questions.q: What service under SPP Doc 203 involves the design of the environment's 'hardscape' and 'softscape,' such as gardens and pavements?
questions.n: This specialized service deals with the exterior environment and its natural/artificial elements.

questions.q: Which service focuses on the physical layout and design of large land areas, such as industrial estates or residential subdivisions?
questions.n: Physical planning involves the large-scale spatial organization of land for various uses.

questions.q: What is 'Architectural Interiors' (AI) as defined under the specialized services of Doc 203?
o: The design of the structural skeleton of the building
The design of the internal space of a building involving finishes and equipment
questions.n: AI focuses on making the interior spaces functional and aesthetically suited for their intended use.

questions.q: Which service involves the detailed design of specialized lighting, acoustics, and communication systems?
questions.n: This specialized service ensures that lighting and sound are technically integrated into the architecture.

questions.q: What service under Doc 203 involves the preservation, restoration, or reconstruction of historic buildings?
questions.n: This specialty focuses on maintaining the cultural and historical value of existing structures.

questions.q: What is the primary responsibility of a Construction Manager (CM) under SPP Doc 204-B?
o: To provide the labor and materials directly
To sign and seal the structural drawings
To coordinate contractors to ensure the project is on time, within budget, and high quality
To pay for the construction costs using their own funds
questions.n: The CM acts as the owner's representative to manage the execution of the work across multiple contractors.

questions.q: Does the Construction Manager (CM) typically assume civil liability for the structural integrity of the building?
o: No, that liability remains with the Architect-of-Record and the Engineers-of-Record
Only if the building is over 15 stories tall
Yes, as the overall manager on site
Yes, if they also act as the general contractor
questions.n: Liability for the design and integrity follows the professional seals on the plans.

questions.q: Which management tool does the CM use to track the progress of work against the planned timeline by identifying the longest sequence of tasks?
questions.n: The Critical Path Method (CPM) is the standard for identifying the tasks that determine the project's finish date.

questions.q: What is the term for the process where the CM reviews the design to find more cost-effective ways to achieve the same result without sacrificing quality?
questions.n: Value Engineering aims to improve the value/cost ratio by finding efficient alternatives for materials or methods.

questions.q: To whom is the Construction Manager directly responsible and accountable?
questions.n: The CM is hired by the Owner to protect their interests during the construction phase.

questions.q: In SPP Doc 301, what is the 'Notice to Proceed'?
o: The architect's approval of shop drawings
The written notice issued by the Owner to the Contractor fixing the start date of work
The building permit from the City Hall
questions.n: This document officially triggers the 'Contract Time' and the contractor's mobilization.

questions.q: What is the term for the sum of money held back from the contractor’s billings to ensure the completion of the work?
questions.n: Usually 10%, this amount is released only after final acceptance and the filing of a guarantee bond.

questions.q: Within how many days must the Architect issue a Certificate of Payment after receiving a request from the contractor?
questions.n: The architect has one week to inspect the site and verify the billing before certifying it for the owner.

questions.q: What is defined as the 'Contract Time' in the general conditions?
o: The time spent in court for legal disputes
The time the architect spends drafting
The period of time allowed in the contract for the completion of the work
questions.n: This includes the total duration from the start date to the substantial completion date.

questions.q: What is a 'Change Order' in the context of SPP Doc 301?
o: A new architectural style for the building
A written order authorizing an adjustment in the work, price, or time
The architect's instruction to the office staff
Changing the lunch break for workers
questions.n: Change orders are the legal mechanism to modify the contract after it has been signed.

questions.q: What is FALAR 1 (Fire Assessment Report 1) as mandated by RA 9514?
o: A report after a fire has occurred
A bill for fire extinguisher refills
A report prepared by the Architect during design documenting fire safety features
A report on fire drill success
questions.n: FALAR 1 is submitted during the building permit stage to prove the design is fire-safe.

questions.q: What is FALAR 2 (Fire Assessment Report 2) which is submitted after the building is built?
o: A report certifying that fire safety features were installed as planned
A list of fire exits that were removed
A certificate from the fire truck manufacturer
questions.n: FALAR 2 is prepared by the Contractor/CM to confirm the actual construction matches the fire code plans.

questions.q: What is the purpose of FALAR 3 (Fire Assessment Report 3)?
o: To report the cause of an arson attack
To calculate the temperature of a flame
To document the annual maintenance of fire safety systems
To design a new fire station
questions.n: Prepared by the building administrator, it ensures that sprinklers, alarms, and exits are still working years later.

questions.q: What is the FSIC (Fire Safety Inspection Certificate)?
o: A receipt for fire code fines
The final certificate confirming a building is safe for occupancy after inspection
A temporary pass for construction workers
questions.n: The BFP issues this after verifying that the building matches the FALAR 2 and code requirements.

questions.q: What is the FSEC (Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance)?
o: A map of the nearest fire hydrants
The clearance issued before the building permit is released
Permission to burn trash on site
questions.n: The BFP evaluates the plans (FALAR 1) and issues the FSEC to allow the local building official to issue a permit.
